I started two tasks, both queued to run now and both scoped to finish within an hour and end in a PR:

1. **"Make agent-user.test.ts pass under any umask"** (test-hardening goal). Two cases fail under umask 077 because the test files' modes depend on the environment. The fix is to set each test file's mode explicitly. If the product code itself relies on the umask, that's a security bug and gets fixed in the code instead. Proof is a pass under both 022 and 077, plus the `security` sub-suite.
2. **"Review Local drivers phase 2 (575cabfa9) against the repo rules and fix what it finds"** (code-review goal). That commit went straight to main and no PR review or PR checks ever saw it. The review checks it against the repo's main rules (egress chokepoint, Capability Contract, descriptions, test placement, diagrams), fixes the small breaks and logs the bigger ones. It opens a PR either way, even if it only records a clean review.

I'll check both reports for the open PR and that each stayed small. Three changes to avoid overlap:
- The WhatsApp undo thread no longer handles the umask test; I told it.
- The larger review draft now skips phase 2.
- Neither new task touches the WhatsApp files.

Still waiting on your approval: the larger review, the chat-thinking flake fix and the nightly triage.

Open questions:

1. **"WhatsApp undo: refuse negated requests and keep documents edited since the save"**: Codex is logged out on dev-madrid. How do you want to unblock it? Only the final test run is left now; the umask fix has its own task.
   - A) I'll log Codex in on dev-madrid (run `codex login --device-auth`; I resume the thread on Codex)
   - B) Finish it on Claude instead (a new thread on Claude continues from the same branch)
   - C) Ship as is (push the committed fix now)

The thread **"Make agent-user.test.ts pass under any umask"** stopped on an infrastructure error ("The hub returned an invalid response"), not on anything in its own work. I sent it a resume message: keep what's already in the worktree and continue to the PR. The message is queued for its next turn. If it fails the same way again, I'll restart the task on a new thread.
